verdict.reasoning: Patient reports soreness in fingers, very bad on hands, with cracked skin on palms and itch: 'soreness in my fingers... the skin on my hands is kind of cracked', 'the palm', 'it's itchy'; duration 'a couple of months ago. I got it three, four months ago.' Pain is implied by 'it hurts a lot.'

Itch is intermittent: 'Yeah, it's itchy. Not all the time, but yeah, it does get itchy.' Bleeding only with scratching: 'yeah I guess when I scratched it, yes it has bled sometimes but, yeah. Otherwise, it hasn't bled on its own.'
Patient notes mild generalized dryness on legs: 'I have dryness, like you know, in other parts, like my legs. But it's not... it's not severe.' and 'Yeah. It's not really, it's not really major.'

Denies systemic symptoms: 'Any other symptoms, such as fever, or temperatures? Patient: No. Any nausea, or any vomiting? Patient: No. Any problem with your bowels? Patient: No. Any problem with your urine, or waterworks? Patient: No.' Appetite and general wellbeing: 'Otherwise you feel well, do you?... your appetite is well-maintained? Patient: Yeah.'
Impact on work: 'Have your symptoms stopped you from doing any work? ... Patient: Uh, yeah like the past three days, I haven't been able to go to work.'
Past medical history: 'Patient: I have diabetes.' 'Do you know if that's type one or type two? Patient: Type two.'
Medication list: 'Which medications do you take? ... Doctor: Metformin, OK.'

Prior treatments: 'have you tried anything over the counter? Any creams? Patient: Yeah. I tried uh E forty five.' and 'I also tried an antihistamine, antihistamine. Uh but it didn't' with doctor acknowledging. Lack of benefit: 'Yeah, no it didn't really do anything.'
Allergies: 'Do you have any allergies, either to any medications or in general? Patient: No.' This supports no known drug allergies.

Family history: 'Family history-wise, is there anything I should be aware of? Patient: Diabetes and what? Doctor: Diabetes as well.' and 'Again, any skin problems? ... Patient: Uh no, not that I know of.'
Job and timing: 'I do work as a housekeeper.' and later 'At a hotel. I have to do the whole thing like bedrooms, bathrooms.' plus 'I switched jobs, uh four months ago.'

Exposure and glove use: 'And to be honest, I'm not always very good about wearing gloves. So that could be related.' and doctor asking about relationship to products; patient: 'Yeah, I usually use those for bathrooms. But, yeah bedrooms and corridors not always.' indicating frequent cleaning chemical use with inconsistent gloves.
Smoking and alcohol: 'Do you smoke at all? Patient: No.' 'Do you drink much in the way of alcohol? ... Patient: Uh, a couple of pints a week.' Doctor: 'OK so, very minimal, alcohol there.'

Assessment: 'I think you might have something called dermatitis or contact dermatitis... particularly people in your... field, who are using cleaning products, not using gloves. And sometimes you get a bit of reaction between the chemicals and your skin.' This links hand dermatitis to irritant cleaning agents and glove non-use.
Type 2 diabetes is a comorbidity by definition of past history: 'I have diabetes.' ... 'Type two.' There is no suggestion it’s the primary problem; it coexists with the dermatitis.
Advice: 'what we try and do is, you know, avoid the triggers. In your case, I strongly recommend that you wear gloves when cleaning at all times.'
Topical steroid: 'we can try some steroid creams to help with the inflammation.'

Emollient frequency and duration: 'As well as some stronger emollients, um which you really need to kind of coat on, three four times a day, for the next couple of weeks.' 'Next couple of weeks' aligns with 10–14 days.
Prescription dispatch: 'I'll I'll I'll do a prescription for you now, and send it over to your pharmacy.'

Follow-up instructions: 'if it still hasn't got better in about a week, two weeks time, I really need you to come back and see me again.' and later 'if it still hasn't got better, or indeed if it's getting worse, like if it's spreading, or dryness is getting worse, come back and see me sooner.'
